Issues.Title: refactor(docs-infra): load doc content with router resources instead of resolvers
Issues.Body:
Enable `withRouterResources()` and load the content of docs, tutorial, CLI and API reference pages through a route `resources` function instead of a `docContent` resolver.

- Replace the `contentResolver()` helper from `@angular/docs` with `contentResource()`, which creates a `resource()` that loads the content through `DOCS_CONTENT_LOADER`. The resource stays idle with an `undefined` value when there is no content path, matching the previous resolver.
- `mapNavigationItemsToRoutes` now defines `resources` instead of `resolve` (keeping a `resources` function passed in the additional route properties). The content path is read from `ctx.data()` rather than captured in a closure: `ReuseTutorialsRouteStrategy` reuses the activated route between tutorial steps, which keeps the resources of the first step and only updates the route data, so reading it reactively makes the resource fetch the content of the new step.
- The CLI and API reference routes use `contentResource()` for their fixed content paths.

The resources are blocking, so the behavior is unchanged: navigation still waits for the content before activating the route (no loading state in the docs viewer, view transitions and prerendering see the full content), and the resolved value is bound to the existing `docContent` inputs. A failed load still fails the navigation with a `NavigationError`; the resource does not wrap `HttpErrorResponse` since it is error-like, so the navigation error handler keeps redirecting to `/404`. Query param only navigations (e.g. the API reference list filters) don't refetch, since the resource only tracks the content path.

This relies on the tutorial page reading its content from the `docContent` input, since resource values are not part of the route `data`.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "refactor(docs-infra): load doc content with router resources instead of resolvers" (#71533)

Issues.Title: fix(common): allow pixel values in NgOptimizedImage sizes alongside responsive values
Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)
- [ ] Docs have been added / updated (for bug fixes / features)

## PR Type

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

Issue Number: #59495

In dev mode, `NgOptimizedImage` throws NG02952 when any source size in `sizes` has a pixel slot width, unless `ngSrcset` is set. The check is a regex that looks for a pixel value at the start of the string or after `, ` or `) `. As a result:

- `sizes="(max-width: 540px) 100vw, (max-width: 960px) 50vw, 370px"`, the case from the issue, throws even though the generated srcset works for it.
- `sizes="min(100vw, 600px)"` throws because the regex sees `, 600px` inside the function.

## What is the new behavior?

This picks up #67070, which took the same direction and was closed as stale. Instead of adding a second regex that looks for `vw` anywhere in the string, it parses `sizes`, so a responsive unit inside a media condition does not count as a responsive slot width. It also covers the review note there about leading whitespace, since `sizes="  500px"` slipped past the old regex.

This follows the heuristic suggested in https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/59495#issuecomment-3874676280: accept pixel values when `sizes` also has responsive values, and keep rejecting sizes that are "basically `500px, 600px`".

The check now splits `sizes` into source sizes on commas outside parentheses, and takes each one's slot width as its last whitespace-separated token outside parentheses. It throws only when every slot width is a plain pixel length:

| `sizes` | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `500px` | throws | throws |
| `  500px` (leading spaces) | allowed | throws |
| `(min-width: 768px) 500px, 300px` | throws | throws |
| `(max-width: 540px) 100vw, (max-width: 960px) 50vw, 370px` | throws | allowed |
| `(min-width: 768px) 500px, 100vw` | throws | allowed |
| `min(100vw, 600px)` | throws | allowed |
| `calc(100vw - 32px)` | allowed | allowed |

When every slot width is in pixels, the image is fixed-size, so the error message now also suggests removing `sizes` to get the density-based srcset generated from `width`.

The two existing "complex `sizes`" tests used `(min-width: 768px) 500px, 100vw`, which is now allowed. They now use a pixel-only value, and new tests cover the allowed cases above. 8 of the new tests fail without this change.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

The check only runs in dev mode, so production bundles are unaffected. The new parser also catches two pixel-only forms the old regex missed, a decimal like `370.5px` and a value with leading whitespace. Those now get the dev-mode error, which is what the check intended for them.

No docs change seemed necessary, since the image optimization guide does not describe this restriction.

Tested on current `main` with `pnpm bazel test //packages/common/test:test` (676 specs, 0 failures).

Supersedes #71070, which was closed because the CLA wasn't signed. The CLA is now signed and the commit author matches it. This is the same change, rebased onto current `main`.

Issues.Title: docs: remove unsupported attributes from kitchen sink tables
Issues.Body:
The kitchen sink documents two attributes that don't exist in the code block pipeline:

- `diff` in the `<docs-code>` table. Nothing in `docs-code.mts`, `docs-code-block.mts` or the formatters reads it, so adding it to a block does nothing.
- `hideDollar` in the `<docs-code-multifile>` table. The multifile extension only parses `hideCode`, `path` and `preview`. `hideDollar` is supported on `<docs-code>` and on code blocks, and stays documented in that table.

Issues.Title: build: patch aspect_rules_jasmine to support test sharding in Jasmine 7
Issues.Body:
In Jasmine 7 (`jasmine-core` 7.0+), `require('jasmine-core')` boots immediately at `require()` time and no longer exposes `jasmine.boot` or `jasmine.Order`. As a result, `@aspect_rules_jasmine` (v2.0.4)'s `runner.cjs` sharding monkey-patches were silent no-ops while still touching `TEST_SHARD_STATUS_FILE`, causing every shard of every `jasmine_test` target to execute 100% of specs in the target and trigger widespread CI timeouts.

This commit adds a `single_version_override` patch for `aspect_rules_jasmine` that configures `specFilter` on the Jasmine environment after specs are loaded when running on Jasmine 7+.

Upstream fix: https://github.com/aspect-build/rules_jasmine/pull/207
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed or merged PR "build: patch aspect_rules_jasmine to support test sharding in Jasmine 7" (#71526)

## What is the current behavior?

The sidecar RPC client uses `any` for method parameters and response types. This allows invalid RPC calls and incorrect result types to pass TypeScript compilation, despite the Rust sidecar expecting specific request and response shapes.

Additionally, responses without a `result` or `error` can silently resolve with `undefined`.

Issue Number: N/A

## What is the new behavior?

- Introduces a typed RPC method map that associates each method with its parameters and return type.
- Infers RPC result types automatically instead of requiring explicit type arguments.
- Replaces unsafe JSON parsing with `unknown` and narrows response fields before accessing them.
- Rejects malformed RPC responses that contain neither a result nor an error.
- Adds an integration test covering file reads and updates through the Rust sidecar.

The existing RPC protocol and public Angular APIs remain unchanged.

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>paulmillr/chokidar (chokidar)</summary>

### [`v6.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#600-2026-10-19)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/compare/5.0.0...6.0.0)

##### High-level changes

- Rewrote the watcher around a single observation pipeline. Backend callbacks are treated as invalidations and confirmed with `lstat`, `stat`, or `readdir` before any event is emitted, so the final state after a burst of changes matches the filesystem.
- Added native recursive watching through `fs.watch({ recursive: true })`. The default `auto` backend uses it on macOS and Windows and per-directory watching elsewhere.
- Shared native handles across watchers and opened them per directory only: files no longer own handles. This fixes `EBADF` errors when watching many files on macOS ([#​1385](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1385), [#​1452](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1452)).
- Replaced `fs.watchFile` with Chokidar-owned stat polling. Poll loops are shared across watchers at the fastest requested interval.
- Required Node.js 22.22 or later.

##### API changes

- Added the `backend` option: `'auto'` (default), `'native'`, `'native-recursive'`, or `'polling'`.
  - `usePolling: true` remains as a deprecated alias for `backend: 'polling'`.
- Renamed `interval` and `binaryInterval` to `pollingInterval` and `pollingBinaryInterval`.
  - The old names remain as deprecated aliases; the new names win when both are given.
- Changed the `atomic` default to `false` with polling. An explicit value is preserved.
- Made `close()` terminal: `add()` now throws once closing has started. Construct a new watcher instead.
- Validated options in the constructor: invalid `backend`, `atomic`, `depth`, `awaitWriteFinish`, and polling intervals throw `TypeError`.
- Emitted errors from `add()` as `error` events instead of unhandled rejections ([#​1378](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1378)).
- Made `getWatched()` return a null-prototype object, so a watched directory named `__proto__` is listed ([#​1493](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1493)). Use `Object.hasOwn()` instead of `hasOwnProperty()` on the result.
- Stopped applying `ignored` to directories above a path passed to `watch()` or `add()`, so a missing path is still watched through its parent ([#​1374](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1374)). Other entries in those directories are still filtered.

##### Fixes

- Fixed a 100% CPU loop when the process working directory containing a relatively watched file was deleted ([#​1474](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1474)).
- Fixed watching a filesystem root, which emitted `unlink` and `unlinkDir` for every entry ([#​1184](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1184), [#​452](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/452)).

Issues.Title: fix(core): remove early event listeners after replay
Issues.Body:
Please note that this fixes a **real** production issue; it wasn't found speculatively through AI code analysis.

In one of our applications, we saw memory growing with event replay enabled, while removing `withEventReplay()` always made the issue go away.

We then found that the `<body>` event listeners added through the inline event dispatch script were never removed. Angular replayed the early events and dropped `window._ejsas[appId]`, but those listeners were still pushing events to the old queue. Nothing was reading that queue again (in the global script).

With this fix, we remove these event listeners right after event replay + when the app is destroyed.

Closes #71518

Issues.Title: Event replay: early event contract listeners on <body> are never removed after hydration
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug?

core

### Is this a regression?

No

### Description

When event replay is enabled (`provideClientHydration(withEventReplay())`), the server adds an inline script to the page:

```js
window.__jsaction_bootstrap(document.body, "ng", ["click"], []);
```

This script adds listeners to `<body>`. They store each event in a queue, `window._ejsas[appId].q`, so Angular can replay events that happen before the app has loaded.

After hydration, Angular replays this queue once and sets `window._ejsas[appId]` to `undefined`. From then on, Angular handles events with its own listeners.

But the inline script's `<body>` listeners are never removed. They keep pushing every event into the same queue, and nothing reads it again. Each entry holds the event and its target element. So:

- the queue grows with every click, for the whole life of the page;
- elements removed from the page later (for example, after a route change) can't be garbage collected if they were ever clicked.

### Cause

In `packages/core/src/hydration/event_replay.ts`, `initEventReplay()` replays the early events and calls `clearAppScopedEarlyEventContract(appId)`, but never calls `removeAllAppScopedEventListeners(appId)`. The same happens in the `appRef.onDestroy()` callback, for an app destroyed before it becomes stable.

For comparison, `EventContract.replayEarlyEvents()` in `@angular/core/primitives/event-dispatch` removes the early listeners right after it replays the events.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Clone the repro and run:
   ```bash
   pnpm install
   pnpm build
   pnpm serve:ssr:event-replay-body-listeners-repro
   ```
2. Open http://localhost:4200.
3. Click the button, or anywhere on the page, a few times.

**Actual:** "Early event queue size" goes up by 1 on every click.

**Expected:** it stays 0 after hydration.


### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug

https://github.com/arturovt/event-replay-body-listeners-repro

### Please provide the exception or error you saw

```true
there's no error, memory grows because every event after hydration is added to `window._ejsas[appId].q` (captured by the early <body> listeners), and nothing reads or clears it
```

### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`)

```true
Angular           : 22.2.3
```

### Anything else?

Related:

- #59261: elements retained by the early event contract after the app is destroyed. The fix (#66371) clears `window._ejsas[appId]`, but the `<body>` listeners still hold the queue, so this part was missed.
- #66506: a different event replay leak (the stashed listener map). Different cause.

Issues.Body:
## PR Checklist

Please check if your PR fulfills the following requirements:

- [x] The commit message follows our guidelines: https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/main/contributing-docs/commit-message-guidelines.md
- [x] Tests for the changes have been added (for bug fixes / features)

What kind of change does this PR introduce?

- [x] Bugfix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Code style update (formatting, local variables)
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes, no api changes)
- [ ] Build related changes
- [ ] CI related changes
- [ ] Documentation content changes
- [ ] angular.dev application / infrastructure changes
- [ ] Other... Please describe:

## What is the current behavior?

`isStartOfRegex` treats any operator token before a `/` as the start of a regular expression, including the postfix `++` and `--`. So `half = count++ / 2` fails with "Unterminated regular expression", and `count-- / size / 2` lexes ` size ` as a regex body.

Issue Number: Fixes #71509

## What is the new behavior?

`++` and `--` now follow the same rule as `!`: when they're postfix, i.e. right after an identifier, a `)`, a `]` or another postfix operator, a slash after them is a division. When they're prefix, the slash can still start a regex, so `++/a/.lastIndex` keeps working. The postfix check is a small helper shared by the three operators. As a side effect, stacked non-null assertions like `a!! / 2` are now read as a division too; they had the same problem.

I added lexer specs for the postfix cases (including `a!++ / 2`) and for the prefix one, plus `checkAction` cases in the parser specs. The postfix specs fail without the change. `//packages/compiler/test/...` passes, and so do the ngtsc and compliance targets, NGP variants included.

## Does this PR introduce a breaking change?

- [ ] Yes
- [x] No

## Other information

Only the 22.3.0-next releases have the update operators, so nothing stable is affected.

Issues.Title: A division right after `++` or `--` in a template is read as a regular expression
Issues.Body:
### Which @angular/* package(s) are the source of the bug? compiler ### Is this a regression? No ### Description Since templates support `++` and `--` (#70816), a slash that follows them is read as the start of a regular expression literal instead of a division: ```html ``` ``` Parser Error: Unexpected token 'Lexer Error: Unterminated regular expression at column 18 in expression [half = count++ / 2]' at column 19 in [half = count++ / 2] ``` With a second slash it gets stranger: in `total = count-- / size / 2`, ` size ` becomes the body of a regex and the parser reports `Unexpected token ' size '`. Host listeners behave the same way. This is valid JavaScript, and `count++ * 2` works fine. The lexer's `isStartOfRegex` treats any operator before a `/` as the start of a regex. That's right after `=` or `&&`, but after `++` or `--` a slash can only be a division. Wrapping the update in parentheses works around it: `(count++) / 2`. #71510 fixes it. Only the 22.3.0-next releases are affected, since 22.2.x doesn't have the update operators. ### Please provide a link to a minimal reproduction of the bug No hosted reproduction, but this is enough: ```ts import {Component} from '@angular/core'; import {bootstrapApplication} from '@angular/platform-browser'; @Component({ selector: 'app-root', template: `

Count: {{ count }}

Half: {{ half }}

`, }) export class App { count = 10; half: number | null = null; } bootstrapApplication(App); ``` ### Please provide the exception or error you saw ```true NG5002: Parser Error: Unexpected token 'Lexer Error: Unterminated regular expression at column 18 in expression [half = count++ / 2]' at column 19 in [half = count++ / 2] NG5002: Parser Error: Lexer Error: Unterminated regular expression at column 18 in expression [half = count++ / 2] at the end of the expression [half = count++ / 2] ``` ### Please provide the environment you discovered this bug in (run `ng version`) ```true @angular/compiler 22.3.0-next.2, and main (d0b33ad25f). ``` ### Anything else? _No response_

### Release Notes

<details>
<summary>paulmillr/chokidar (chokidar)</summary>

### [`v6.0.0`](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/blob/HEAD/CHANGELOG.md#600-2026-10-19)

[Compare Source](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/compare/5.0.0...6.0.0)

##### High-level changes

- Rewrote the watcher around a single observation pipeline. Backend callbacks are treated as invalidations and confirmed with `lstat`, `stat`, or `readdir` before any event is emitted, so the final state after a burst of changes matches the filesystem.
- Added native recursive watching through `fs.watch({ recursive: true })`. The default `auto` backend uses it on macOS and Windows and per-directory watching elsewhere.
- Shared native handles across watchers and opened them per directory only: files no longer own handles. This fixes `EBADF` errors when watching many files on macOS ([#​1385](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1385), [#​1452](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1452)).
- Replaced `fs.watchFile` with Chokidar-owned stat polling. Poll loops are shared across watchers at the fastest requested interval.
- Required Node.js 22.22 or later.

##### API changes

- Added the `backend` option: `'auto'` (default), `'native'`, `'native-recursive'`, or `'polling'`.
  - `usePolling: true` remains as a deprecated alias for `backend: 'polling'`.
- Renamed `interval` and `binaryInterval` to `pollingInterval` and `pollingBinaryInterval`.
  - The old names remain as deprecated aliases; the new names win when both are given.
- Changed the `atomic` default to `false` with polling. An explicit value is preserved.
- Made `close()` terminal: `add()` now throws once closing has started. Construct a new watcher instead.
- Validated options in the constructor: invalid `backend`, `atomic`, `depth`, `awaitWriteFinish`, and polling intervals throw `TypeError`.
- Emitted errors from `add()` as `error` events instead of unhandled rejections ([#​1378](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1378)).
- Made `getWatched()` return a null-prototype object, so a watched directory named `__proto__` is listed ([#​1493](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1493)). Use `Object.hasOwn()` instead of `hasOwnProperty()` on the result.
- Stopped applying `ignored` to directories above a path passed to `watch()` or `add()`, so a missing path is still watched through its parent ([#​1374](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1374)). Other entries in those directories are still filtered.

##### Fixes

- Fixed a 100% CPU loop when the process working directory containing a relatively watched file was deleted ([#​1474](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1474)).
- Fixed watching a filesystem root, which emitted `unlink` and `unlinkDir` for every entry ([#​1184](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1184), [#​452](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/452)).
- Fixed `UNKNOWN` errors from `fs.watch` on macOS sockets, which prevented watching `/var/run` ([#​1391](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1391)).
- Fixed a symlink whose target passes through a regular file (`ENOTDIR`) disabling watching of its directory and preventing `ready` ([#​1476](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1476)).
- Fixed files created in a newly added directory between its scan and watch registration being missed ([#​1471](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1471)).
- Fixed watching a missing nested path stopping its parent directory's subtree from being watched ([#​1470](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1470)).
- Fixed false `change` events on Windows when many sibling files are written ([#​1466](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1466)).
- Fixed duplicate `add` events for unchanged files under directory activity ([#​1465](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1465)).
- Fixed replacing a watched directory with a file of the same name hanging the process ([#​1464](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1464)).
- Fixed persistent watching stopping after a watched directory was removed ([#​1463](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1463)).
- Fixed a deleted watched path not being reported when recreated: previously only a deleted file that was the sole watched path was watched for its return. Any path passed to `watch()` or `add()` is now awaited from its nearest existing parent.
- Fixed event throttling discarding updates; the newest differing change is now replayed when the window closes ([#​1455](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1455)).
- Fixed relative `ignored` paths; relative strings now resolve against `cwd` or the process working directory ([#​1436](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1436)).
- Fixed files not being detected when their directory did not exist before watching ([#​1422](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1422)).
- Fixed removed files being reported as `unlinkDir` instead of `unlink` ([#​1421](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1421)).
- Fixed ignored files and directories still being watched in WSL ([#​1418](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1418)).
- Fixed `change` being reported for every file when one file changed under Deno ([#​1417](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1417)).
- Fixed changes not being detected after the second save ([#​1399](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1399)).
- Fixed renaming a watched directory that contains subdirectories on Windows ([#​1380](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1380), [#​1398](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1398)).
- Fixed re-watching a path not honoring `ignoreInitial` ([#​1386](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1386)).
- Fixed `EISDIR` errors during the initial scan of network drives ([#​1376](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1376)).
- Fixed watching an array of absolute file paths ([#​1366](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1366)).

- Documented that unwatched paths stay ignored until they are added again ([#​1439](https://redirect.github.com/paulmillr/chokidar/issues/1439)).

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): preserve asset precedence and expand glob-prefixed ignores in watch mode
Issues.Body:
Previously in library watch mode, ignore patterns containing glob characters that did not end with `*` (such as `**/<dir>` or `{a,b}`) were not expanded with `/**` because `normalizeGlobPattern` checked `picomatch.scan(result).isGlob`. Update `normalizeGlobPattern` to append `/**` whenever the stripped pattern does not end with `*`, matching `tinyglobby` directory expansion semantics.

In `collectAssetsToEmit`, incremental watch builds previously only deduplicated colliding output paths among files present in the current `modifiedFiles` set. Modifying a lower-priority asset could therefore overwrite an existing higher-priority asset on disk, and deleting a higher-priority asset did not restore an existing lower-priority fallback asset. Resolve candidate sources across all asset matchers, evict overridden asset sources in `BuilderState.recordEmittedOutputs`, and re-emit lower-priority fallback assets when an overriding asset is deleted. Also preserve cached `statSync` results during deleted-directory checks so a newly created file replacing a directory at the same path is still matched and emitted.

Issues.Title: `ng generate component/directive --module` declares a class that doesn't exist when `addTypeToClassName` is `false`
Issues.Body:
### Command

generate

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

The `addTypeToClassName` option was added in 21.0.0, and the declaration code was not updated, so it never worked.

### Description

When a component or directive is generated into an NgModule with `addTypeToClassName: false` and a `type` set, the
generated class and the symbol added to the NgModule don't match:

- The component/directive class is named without the type (e.g. `Widget`), as configured.
- The NgModule `declarations` (and `exports` with `--export`) import the name **with** the type
  (e.g. `WidgetComponent`), so the build fails.

This is the configuration that `ng new --no-standalone --file-name-style-guide=2016` writes to `angular.json`:

```json
"@schematics/angular:component": { "type": "component", "addTypeToClassName": false },
"@schematics/angular:directive": { "type": "directive", "addTypeToClassName": false }
```

The component and directive schematics compute the class name with `addTypeToClassName`
(`packages/schematics/angular/component/index.ts`, `packages/schematics/angular/directive/index.ts`), but the shared
`addDeclarationToNgModule` helper always appends the type:

```ts
// packages/schematics/angular/utility/add-declaration-to-ng-module.ts
const classifiedName =
  strings.classify(options.name) + (options.type ? strings.classify(options.type) : '');
```


### Minimal Reproduction

```sh
ng new ws --no-standalone --file-name-style-guide=2016 --defaults
cd ws
ng generate component widget --module app
ng build
```


Generated `src/app/widget/widget.component.ts`:

```ts
export class Widget {}
```

Updated `src/app/app.module.ts`:

```ts
import { WidgetComponent } from './widget/widget.component';

@NgModule({
  declarations: [App, WidgetComponent],
```

The same happens for `ng generate directive ... --module`.


### Exception or Error

```text
✘ [ERROR] TS2305: Module '"./widget/widget.component"' has no exported member 'WidgetComponent'. [plugin angular-compiler]
✘ [ERROR] NG1010: Value at position 1 in the NgModule.declarations of AppModule is not a reference
```

### Your Environment

```text
Angular CLI       : 22.2.3
Node.js           : 24.15.0
Package Manager   : npm 11.12.1
Operating System  : darwin arm64
@schematics/angular : 22.2.3
```

### Anything else relevant?

- Introduced together with `addTypeToClassName` in e417c89f9e (#31053, v21.0.0). The same code is on `21.2.x` and `22.2.x`.
- Suggested fix: let `addDeclarationToNgModule` use the class name computed by the calling schematic (or honour
  `addTypeToClassName`), so the declaration matches the generated class. Happy to send a PR with specs for the
  component and directive schematics.

Issues.Body:
### Command

serve

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

See https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-698v-4r3x-3vcv (CVE-2026-112943, CVSS v4 6.3): "launch-editor: escapeCmdArgs() omits % escaping on Windows". vite bundles `launch-editor` into its dist, so the fix only ships with a vite bump.

Affected ranges relevant here: `vite >= 8.3.0, <= 8.3.2` (patched in `8.3.3`) and `vite >= 7.0.0, <= 7.3.6` (patched in `7.3.7`).

`@angular/build` pins a vulnerable version exactly on the active and both LTS branches:

Issues.Title: fix(@angular/build): rebuild stylesheets when files are added to a PostCSS directory dependency
Issues.Body:
Previously, a PostCSS `dir-dependency` message (used by Tailwind CSS v4 for its content sources) was expanded with a glob and only the files that existed at build time were watched. Files created later, or moved by renaming their folder, did not invalidate the cached stylesheet, so classes used only in them were not generated until the stylesheet itself changed.

The directory is now also added to the watch files, and the load result cache invalidates an entry when a changed path is inside one of its watched directories.

Fixes #34446

Issues.Title: `ng generate app-shell` and `ng generate module --route` produce broken imports when a component `type` is configured
Issues.Body:
### Command

generate

### Is this a regression?

- [x] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

19.x (before the v20 file naming change)

### Description

`ng generate app-shell` and `ng generate module <name> --route <path> --module <parent>` generate a component and then
reference it with a hard-coded file path and class name. Both assume the v20+ defaults (no type in the file or class
name). When the workspace configures a component `type`, the component inherits it and the hard-coded references no
longer match, so the build fails.

Workspaces get a component `type` in two common ways:

1. Every workspace updated to v20 with `ng update`: the migration that keeps the previous style guide behaviour
   (fdc6291dda) adds `"@schematics/angular:component": { "type": "component" }`.
2. `ng new --file-name-style-guide=2016`, which adds `{ "type": "component", "addTypeToClassName": false }`.

Hard-coded references:

- `packages/schematics/angular/app-shell/index.ts`: `withAppShell(AppShell)` and
  `insertImport(..., 'AppShell', './app-shell/app-shell')`.

### Description

Issues.Title: fix(material/datepicker): clear invalid text when the form value is reset
Issues.Body:
Fixes #33978.

## Problem

`writeValue` skipped re-formatting the input when the incoming value was the same as the current one. This was added in #32447 and #32485 to work around signal forms writing the same value back into the CVA while the user was typing (#32442, #32475).

As a side effect, an unparseable value could no longer be cleared programmatically. After the user types something like `foo`, the model value is `null`, so `reset()` / `setValue(null)` calls `writeValue(null)` with the value that's already there and gets skipped. The invalid text stays in the input, and because `_lastValueValid` is reset, no `matDatepickerParse` error is shown either. Signal forms `reset()` goes through the same path and is affected as well.

## Fix

Angular 22.0.0 deduplicates `writeValue` calls in the CVA interop (angular/angular@2e9aeea0f), and `@angular/material` 22 requires `@angular/core ^22.0.0`, so the workaround is no longer needed. This PR removes it so `writeValue` always re-formats the input, and drops the now-unused `reformat` parameter from `_assignValueProgrammatically`.

## Tests

- Replaced the two reactive forms specs that simulated the old signal forms loopback (and asserted the text is kept) with a spec that `reset()` clears invalid text.
- Added signal forms specs using the real `[formField]` integration:
  - invalid text is not cleared while typing (#32475)
  - a valid date is not re-formatted while typing (#32442)
  - `reset()` clears invalid text

I also checked it manually in an Angular / Material 22.2.3 app, before and after patching:

| Scenario | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Reactive forms: type `foo`, then `reset()` | `foo` stays | cleared |
| Reactive forms: type `bar`, then `setValue(null)` | `bar` stays | cleared |
| Signal forms: type `foo`, then `reset()` | `foo` stays | cleared |
| Signal forms: type `foo` | kept | kept |
| Signal forms: type `1` → `1/` → … → `1/1/2026` | not clobbered | not clobbered |
| Signal forms with `debounce`: same typing sequences | not clobbered | not clobbered |
| Programmatic valid date (reactive and signal) | formatted | formatted |

Issues.Title: bug(aria/combobox): ComboboxPopup throws NG0950 when destroyed before its first change detection
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description `ComboboxPopup.ngOnDestroy` calls `this.combobox()._unregisterPopup()`. The `combobox` input is `input.required()`. If the view that holds the popup is destroyed before its first update pass, the input was never set, and reading it throws `NG0950: Input "combobox" is required but no value is available yet`. Angular reports this as "Error during cleanup of component", and in tests it fails the test ("1 fixture threw errors during cleanup"). This happens in any unit test that creates a component containing a combobox and does not run change detection before teardown, for example a plain "should create" test, or a test that only checks providers. ### Reproduction ```ts import { Component } from '@angular/core'; import { TestBed } from '@angular/core/testing'; import { Combobox, ComboboxPopup, ComboboxWidget } from '@angular/aria/combobox'; import { Listbox, Option } from '@angular/aria/listbox'; @Component({ imports: [Combobox, ComboboxPopup, ComboboxWidget, Listbox, Option], template: `
Pick one
alpha
 `, }) class Repro {} it('destroys cleanly before the first change detection', () => { const fixture = TestBed.createComponent(Repro); expect(() => fixture.destroy()).not.toThrow(); // throws NG0950 }); ``` ### Expected Behavior Destroying the popup without a first change detection does nothing (there is nothing to unregister). ### Actual Behavior `NG0950: Input "combobox" is required but no value is available yet`, from `ComboboxPopup.ngOnDestroy` (`src/aria/combobox/combobox-popup.ts`, line 67 on `main`). A possible fix: register in `ngOnInit` and keep the registered combobox in a field, then unregister that field (if set) in `ngOnDestroy`, instead of reading the input again. Workaround: wrap the `ng-template ngComboboxPopup` in `@if (combobox) { … }`, so the popup is only created in an update pass. ### Environment - Angular: 22.2.1 - CDK/Material: @angular/cdk 22.2.3, @angular/aria 22.2.3 (also in 22.3.0-next.2 and `main`) - Browser(s): any (seen in Vitest with happy-dom) - Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS

Issues.Title: bug(aria/menu): any DOM change inside an open submenu moves focus up and collapses it
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression? - [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version ### The previous version in which this bug was not present was _No response_ ### Description Any DOM change inside an open `ngMenu` (a ripple, an icon that renders late, an `@if` inside an item) moves focus back up the menu tree and collapses the open submenu, even though no menu item was added, removed or moved. What happens: 1. `Menu` starts `_collection.startObserving(this.element)` in `afterNextRender`. The `MutationObserver` in `SortedCollection` bumps `_version` on any `childList` change in the menu's subtree. 2. `orderedItems` has no `equal`, so every bump produces a new array, and `Menu._items` / `_itemPatterns` change identity too. 3. The `afterRenderEffect` in `Menu`'s constructor that calls `this._pattern.listBehavior.goto(activeItem)` tracks the item list by accident: `ListFocus.focus()` reads `inputs.items()` through `isListDisabled()`. So it re-runs and focuses the menu's active item. 4. Focus moves from the open submenu to an item in a menu above it, and `MenuPattern.onFocusOut` closes the submenu. Possible fixes (any one of these avoids it): - Give `SortedCollection.orderedItems` an element-wise `equal`, so a version bump that changes no order isn't propagated. - Read the item list `untracked` in the `goto(activeItem)` effect; it only needs to re-run when `visible()` changes. - Bump `_version` only when an added node contains a registered item (the `TODO(ok7sai)` in `SortedCollection` already plans to replace the observer). ### Reproduction StackBlitz link: not attached. The standalone component below is the whole reproduction; it needs only `@angular/aria` (bootstrapped with `provideZonelessChangeDetection()`). ```ts import { Component, signal } from '@angular/core'; import { Menu, MenuItem, MenuTrigger } from '@angular/aria/menu'; @Component({ selector: 'app-root', imports: [Menu, MenuItem, MenuTrigger], styles: `[data-visible='false'] { opacity: 0.3; }`, template: `
Item A
Item B
Item B1
Item B2
Last item @if (menuB2.visible() && tick() % 2) { • }
`, }) export class App { protected readonly tick = signal(0); constructor() { setInterval(() => this.tick.update((n) => n + 1), 1000); } } ``` Steps to reproduce: 1. Focus **Open** and press Enter. 2. Press ArrowDown, ArrowRight, ArrowDown, ArrowRight. Focus is now on **Last item**, with both submenus open. 3. Wait up to a second, until the `@if` renders its dot. ### Expected Behavior The submenus stay open and focus stays on **Last item**: the change adds no menu item, so the menu state shouldn't change. ### Actual Behavior **Item B2** collapses (`aria-expanded="false"`) and focus moves to **Item B2**. Without the `@if` (or with the interval removed), both submenus stay open and focus stays on **Last item**. It reproduces every time, and the same way with a third submenu level. ### Environment - Angular: 22.1.4 - CDK/Material: @angular/cdk 22.1.4; @angular/aria 22.1.4 and 22.2.3 (the code involved is unchanged in 22.3.0-next.2) - Browser(s): Chromium 153 - Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): macOS

Fixes #33973.

`ComboboxPattern` relays keys to the popup through a signal that holds only the latest event, and an effect re-dispatches it later. When two keys arrived before the effect ran, the first was overwritten and never reached the popup, so quick Down, Down, Down moved once and fast typeahead lost characters.

The key handlers now queue each event, and the effect dispatches every queued event to the popup in order. I added a spec that sends keys back to back and checks that each one is handled; it fails without the change.

Issues.Title: bug(material/menu): menu restores focus to its trigger after a menu item opens a dialog (animations disabled / prefers-reduced-motion)
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

 When a mat-menu item opens a MatDialog and animations are disabled (provideNoopAnimations / animations disabled, or the user's OS has reduced motion so `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` matches), the dialog ends up with no focus: focus is moved back to the menu trigger behind the dialog's backdrop.

Cause: with animations disabled the dialog's initial focus runs synchronously during the menu item's click (in the microtask after the click listener). The click then reaches the menu panel, which emits `closed('click')`, and `MatMenuTriggerBase._destroyMenu` calls `this.focus(this._openedBy)` unconditionally, without checking where focus currently is. With animations enabled the dialog focuses ~150ms later, after the menu has closed, so the problem doesn't show.

Since `prefers-reduced-motion` comes from an OS setting (e.g. Windows "Animation effects" off), regular users hit this, and keyboard and screen-reader users land on a control hidden behind the modal.

This was reported in #14879, which was closed as a duplicate of #11696 before the reporter clarified it only happens with NoopAnimationsModule; it was then locked. The menu code on `main` still restores focus unconditionally.

Possible fix, following the dialog's own guard from #17300 ("don't move focus if it was moved during close animation"): in `_destroyMenu`, when the close reason is `'click'`, skip restoring focus if it is already inside a different overlay pane (not the menu's own pane, not a menu panel such as a submenu, and not the overlay pane that contains the trigger itself). Every other close (Escape, Tab, backdrop click, programmatic close) keeps today's
behaviour. This doesn't change the accessibility position in #11696: focus still returns to the trigger whenever the menu owns it; it only stops the menu from pulling focus out of a modal that an item just opened. Happy to send a PR with tests if this direction is acceptable.

### Reproduction

  StackBlitz (from #14879, older Angular/Material):
  https://stackblitz.com/edit/checkbox-reactive-2zhjpp?file=app%2Fapp.component.ts

  I wasn't able to save a new StackBlitz, so this links the reproduction from #14879. The bug is not specific to that
  old version:

  - It reproduces on Angular 21.2.25 / @angular/cdk + @angular/material 21.1.2 in an application with animations
  disabled through the OS setting (Windows "Animation effects" off, so `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` matches and
  Material disables its animations). After a menu item opens a MatDialog, `document.activeElement` is the menu trigger
  behind the dialog's backdrop, not the dialog's `cdkFocusInitial` button.
  - The cause is unchanged on `main`: `MatMenuTriggerBase._destroyMenu` in `src/material/menu/menu-trigger-base.ts`
  still ends with

      if (this.restoreFocus && (reason === 'keydown' || !this._openedBy || !this._triggersSubmenu())) {
        this.focus(this._openedBy);
      }

    with no check of where focus currently is, so whenever the dialog takes focus before the menu finishes closing
  (always the case with animations disabled), the menu takes it back.

  Steps (old StackBlitz, which uses NoopAnimations):
  1. Open the StackBlitz and click the menu trigger.
  2. Click the menu item that opens the dialog.
  3. In the console, run `document.activeElement`: it is the menu trigger, not the dialog's button.

  Single-file reproduction for current versions (Angular/Material 21; paste as main.ts in a new Angular project):

  import {Component, inject} from '@angular/core';
  import {bootstrapApplication} from '@angular/platform-browser';
  import {MatButtonModule} from '@angular/material/button';
  import {MatMenuModule} from '@angular/material/menu';
  import {MatDialog, MatDialogModule} from '@angular/material/dialog';

  @Component({
    imports: [MatButtonModule, MatDialogModule],
    template: `
      <mat-dialog-content>Delete this item?</mat-dialog-content>
      <mat-dialog-actions>
        <button mat-button mat-dialog-close cdkFocusInitial>Cancel</button>
        <button mat-button [mat-dialog-close]="true">Delete</button>
      </mat-dialog-actions>
    `,
  })
  export class ConfirmDialog {}

  @Component({
    selector: 'app-root',
    imports: [MatButtonModule, MatMenuModule, MatDialogModule],
    template: `
      <button mat-button [matMenuTriggerFor]="menu">Menu</button>
      <mat-menu #menu="matMenu">
        <button mat-menu-item (click)="open()">Open dialog</button>
      </mat-menu>
    `,
  })
  export class App {
    private dialog = inject(MatDialog);
    open() { this.dialog.open(ConfirmDialog); }
  }

  bootstrapApplication(App);

  On 21, emulate reduced motion (DevTools > Rendering > "Emulate CSS media feature prefers-reduced-motion: reduce", then
  reload) or set the OS animation setting off, then click Menu > Open dialog and check `document.activeElement`.

### Expected Behavior

Focus stays on the dialog's initial focus target (the "Cancel" button with cdkFocusInitial), showing its focus indicator, exactly as it does when animations are enabled. The menu should not move focus back to its trigger while an overlay opened by the menu item holds focus.

### Actual Behavior

The dialog opens, but focus is on the menu trigger ("Menu") behind the dialog's backdrop: document.activeElement is the trigger button with cdk-focused / cdk-mouse-focused. The dialog shows no focused control, Enter re-activates the hidden trigger, and Tab starts from outside the dialog. The dialog's FocusTrap did focus "Cancel" first; the menu's _destroyMenu then called focus() on the trigger. 

document.activeElement after the dialog opens: button.mat-mdc-menu-trigger  (the menu trigger, behind the backdrop)

### Environment

  - Angular: 21.2.25
  - CDK/Material: 21.1.2 (the same unconditional restore is still in src/material/menu/menu-trigger-base.ts on main)
  - Browser(s): Chrome <your version>; also reproduced in an embedded Chromium. Any browser with animations disabled or
  prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.
  - Operating System: Windows 11 (Settings > Accessibility > Visual effects > Animation effects: Off)

Issues.Title: fix(multiple): allow aria tab and accordion panels without content directive
Issues.Body:
The `ngTabPanel` and `ngAccordionPanel` directives warn in dev mode that they need `ngTabContent` or `ngAccordionContent` to render, but content placed directly in a panel already renders. It's created eagerly and stays in the DOM, and the panel gets the `inert` attribute while hidden.

This removes the warning, making eager rendering a supported alternative to the content directive. A single tab group or accordion can then mix eager panels with lazy ones, which keep or remove their content depending on their own `preserveContent`.

Rendering eagerly also means the content is included in server-rendered HTML, unlike lazy content.

Fixes #33950

Issues.Title: bug(aria/tabs): the tab list loses its only Tab stop when the active tab is removed after an interaction
Issues.Body:
### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this behavior used to work in the previous version

### The previous version in which this bug was not present was

_No response_

### Description

When the tab that currently holds the roving `tabindex="0"` (the *active* tab, `TabListPattern.activeTab`) is removed from the tab list after the user has already interacted with the list, **no remaining tab gets `tabindex="0"`**. Every tab ends up with `tabindex="-1"`, so the tab list is no longer reachable with `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` (WCAG 2.1.1 / 2.4.3).

It is easy to hit with `selectionMode="explicit"`, where the active tab (focus) and the selected tab can differ, but the cause does not look specific to it: any removal of the active item after the first interaction should behave the same.

Cause, from reading the source (the guard is still on `main`): `TabListPattern.setDefaultState()` is the only place that re-assigns `activeItem`, and it is guarded.

```js
setDefaultStateEffect() {
  if (this.hasBeenInteracted()) return;   // never runs again after the first interaction
  this.setDefaultState();
}
// onKeydown / onClick / onFocusIn: this.hasBeenInteracted.set(true)
```

After the first focus / key / click, `hasBeenInteracted` stays `true`. If the active tab is then destroyed, `activeItem` still points to the removed tab, so no tab in `items()` matches and the roving `tabindex` is `-1` everywhere. Nothing falls back to the selected tab or to the first focusable tab.

A possible fix is to re-run the default-state logic when the active item is no longer part of `items()`, regardless of `hasBeenInteracted`:

```js
setDefaultStateEffect() {
  const active = this.activeTab();
  if (this.hasBeenInteracted() && active !== undefined && this.inputs.items().includes(active)) return;
  this.setDefaultState();
}
```

Related: #33934 (same area of code, but about a focus moved by a script, not about a removed active tab); #32969 / 0f5b0eee introduced the `hasBeenInteracted` guard.

### Reproduction

StackBlitz link: https://stackblitz.com/edit/duypg9mo?file=src%2Fapp%2Fapp.ts

Steps to reproduce:
1. `Tab` into the tab list (focus lands on `A`), press `ArrowDown` once: focus moves to `B`, which is now the active tab (`tabindex="0"`); `A` stays selected because the selection is explicit.
2. Press `Tab` three times: the panel itself, the input, then the `remove B` button.
3. Press `Enter` on `remove B`: the active tab `B` is destroyed.
4. Inspect the tabs: `A` and `C` both have `tabindex="-1"`.
5. Press `Shift+Tab` repeatedly: focus goes back through the input and the panel, then to the previous focusable element of the page. The tab list is skipped entirely.

Reproduced on `@angular/aria` 22.2.1 and 22.2.3.

### Expected Behavior

After the active tab is removed, a remaining tab (the selected one, else the first focusable) becomes the active tab and gets `tabindex="0"`, so the tab list keeps exactly one Tab stop.

### Actual Behavior

All tabs have `tabindex="-1"`. The tab list cannot be reached with `Tab` / `Shift+Tab`, and the arrow keys cannot help since focus cannot enter the list.

### Environment

- Angular: 22.2.1
- CDK/Material: `@angular/aria` 22.2.1 and 22.2.3, `@angular/cdk` 22.2.1 and 22.2.3
- Browser(s): Microsoft Edge (Chromium), also driven with real key events over the Chrome DevTools Protocol
- Operating System (e.g. Windows, macOS, Ubuntu): Windows 11
